questionText: A moving coil galvanometer has a coil of effective area $A$, number of turns $N$. The magnetic field $B$ is radial. If current $I$ is passed through the coil, the torque acting on the coil is:

options.explanation: Option A ($N A^2 B I$) is inconsistent with canonical textbook criteria.
Option B ($N^2 A^2 B I$) is inconsistent with canonical textbook criteria.
Option C ($N A B I$) is the conceptually verified answer according to NCERT Physics Class 12.

answer_note: Verified with NCERT Physics Class 12 textbook: NCERT Physics Class 12, Chapter: Moving Charges and Magnetism
keyConcept: Moving Charges and Magnetism: Moving Coil Galvanometer Torque

ncert_reference.citation: NCERT Physics Class 12, Chapter: Moving Charges and Magnetism

solution.quick: In a radial magnetic field, the plane of the coil is always parallel to the field lines ($\sin 90^\circ = 1$), so deflecting torque is $\tau = NIAB = NABI$.
solution.concept: The torque on a planar current loop of magnetic moment $\vec{M} = N I \vec{A}$ in magnetic field $\vec{B}$ is $\vec{\tau} = \vec{M} \times \vec{B}$. Concave magnetic poles produce a radial field, ensuring maximum torque $\tau = NIAB$ at all deflections.
solution.step_by_step:
A coil having $N$ turns, area $A$, and carrying current $I$ has magnetic dipole moment:
$$M = N I A$$
The deflecting magnetic torque acting on the coil is:
$$\tau = M B \sin\theta = N I A B \sin\theta$$
where $\theta$ is the angle between the magnetic dipole moment (normal to the coil area) and the magnetic field $\vec{B}$.
In a moving coil galvanometer, cylindrical concave pole pieces and a soft iron cylinder core create a radial magnetic field.
Consequently, the plane of the coil always remains parallel to the magnetic field lines in all positions of deflection, making the normal to the plane perpendicular to the field ($\theta = 90^\circ$):
$$\tau = N I A B \sin 90^\circ = N A B I$$
Hence, option C is correct.

answer_note: Verified with NCERT Physics Class 12 textbook: NCERT Physics Class 12, Chapter: Alternating Current
keyConcept: Alternating Current: Transformer Core Losses and Eddy Currents

ncert_reference.citation: NCERT Physics Class 12, Chapter: Alternating Current

solution.quick: Laminating the transformer core reduces eddy current loops and minimizes heat dissipation ($I^2 R$).
solution.concept: An alternating magnetic flux induces circulating currents (eddy currents) in a solid metallic core. By using thin sheets insulated by varnish, the resistance to circulating current paths is greatly increased, reducing power loss.
solution.step_by_step:
When alternating magnetic flux passes through a solid iron core in a transformer, circulating currents called eddy currents are induced in planes perpendicular to the flux lines. These eddy currents dissipate electrical energy as heat:
$$P_{\text{eddy}} \propto f^2 B_{\max}^2 t^2$$
where $t$ is the thickness of each sheet.
To minimize this loss, the core is constructed from thin sheets of silicon steel (laminations) coated with an insulating varnish. This breaks up continuous conduction loops, increasing resistance and drastically reducing energy loss due to eddy currents.

- The surface area of the sphere is $A = 4\pi R^2$

solution.quick: $H = W_{\text{battery}} = \Delta q \cdot V = (2 C V) V = 2 C V^2 = 2(10 \times 10^{-6})(12^2) = 2.88\text{ mJ}$.
solution.concept: When a capacitor charged to $+Q$ is reconnected with reversed polarity, the charge on each plate must change from $+Q$ to $-Q$. Total charge delivered by the battery is $\Delta q = 2Q = 2CV$. The work done by the battery is $W = \Delta q \cdot V = 2CV^2$. Since stored electrostatic energy before and after is identical ($U_i = U_f = \frac{1}{2}CV^2$), all work done by the battery is dissipated as heat: $H = 2CV^2$.
solution.step_by_step:
Given:
- $C = 10\,\mu\text{F} = 10 \times 10^{-6}\text{ F}$
- $V = 12\text{ V}$

1. Initial and final charges on positive plate:
$$q_i = +C V = +(10 \times 10^{-6})(12) = +120\,\mu\text{C}$$
$$q_f = -C V = -(10 \times 10^{-6})(12) = -120\,\mu\text{C}$$

2. Net charge flown through battery:
$$\Delta q = |q_f - q_i| = 240\,\mu\text{C} = 2 C V$$

3. Work done by the battery:
$$W_{\text{battery}} = \Delta q \cdot V = (2 C V) \cdot V = 2 C V^2$$
$$W_{\text{battery}} = 2 \times (10 \times 10^{-6}) \times (12)^2 = 2 \times 10^{-5} \times 144 = 2.88 \times 10^{-3}\text{ J} = 2.88\text{ mJ}$$

4. Change in electrostatic potential energy stored in capacitor:
